record.paper_title: Achievement sets – current results and open problems
record.context_brief: Possible ranges of the cardinality function
record.original_question: For which subsets C of {0,1,2,…,ω,c} does there exist an absolutely convergent series x such that the associated cardinality function F_x(t), which counts the number of subseries representations of t, has range exactly C?

evidence.quote: The function Fx(t) = card(f^{-1}(t)) is called the cardinality function for x.
For which sets C ⊆ {0, 1, 2, . . . , ω,c} does there exist a sequence x such that the cardinal function Fx has range exactly C?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $x=(x_n)_{n=1}^{\infty}$ be an absolutely convergent series of nonzero real numbers. Define the map
$$f:\{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}\to\mathbb{R},\qquad f(\varepsilon)=\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\varepsilon_n x_n,$$
and for each $t\in\mathbb{R}$ let
$$F_x(t)=\operatorname{card}\bigl(f^{-1}(t)\bigr)\in\{0,1,2,\dots,\omega,\mathfrak{c}\},$$
the number of subseries representations of $t$ (here $\omega$ denotes the countably infinite cardinal $\aleph_0$ and $\mathfrak c$ the cardinality of the continuum; it is known that $F_x(t)$ takes values only in $\{0,1,2,\dots,\omega,\mathfrak c\}$). The range of $F_x$ is the set $\{F_x(t):t\in\mathbb{R}\}\subseteq\{0,1,2,\dots,\omega,\mathfrak c\}$.

Characterize precisely which subsets $C\subseteq\{0,1,2,\dots,\omega,\mathfrak c\}$ arise as the range of $F_x$ for some absolutely convergent series $x$ — i.e., determine all $C$ for which there exists such a sequence $x$ with $\{F_x(t):t\in\mathbb{R}\}=C$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is listed among current open problems on achievement sets and cardinality functions of subseries. A recent preprint "Bounded ranges of cardinal functions" addresses partial cases (bounded ranges) but the full characterization of admissible ranges $C\subseteq\{0,1,\dots,\omega,\mathfrak c\}$ remains unresolved.
